Adversarial journalism remains the frontline defense against corporate consolidation and state propaganda.
Amy Goodman Live Screening: Steal This Story, Please!
Evidence: Press Freedom, Public Broadcasting, Media Accountability
#Aletheia #DemocracyNow #Journalism

Democracy Now! announces an exclusive virtual screening of 'Steal This Story, Please!' and live panel with Amy Goodman, spotlighting three decades of fearless independent grassroots reporting that holds global empires accountable.
Stated Judgement: (+0.94, +0.86) — Greater Good

The production reliably documents Goodman's thirty-year record of non-commercial journalism, though framing an event titled 'Steal This Story' behind a twenty-dollar virtual ticket slightly limits broad public accessibility.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.88, +0.82) — Greater Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Grace. The event faithfully honors thirty years of fearless adversarial reporting that gives voice to marginalized communities and challenges state and corporate power without compromise.
Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.08, Uncertainty z: 0)

- Democracy Now!: PASS (+0.92, +0.86) — 30 years of truth.
- The Documentary: PASS (+0.89, +0.82) — Deep press history.
- Ticket Model: COND (+0.78, +0.65) — $20 fee limits access.
- Amy Goodman: PASS (+0.95, +0.88) — Fearless accountability.

Democracy Now! is hosting a special live broadcast of a new documentary chronicling Amy Goodman's journalism career, followed by a live discussion with Oscar-nominated directors and journalist Maria Hinojosa.

The Poison:
Screening a documentary titled 'Steal This Story, Please!' behind a $19.98 paywall creates a minor irony for an independent newsroom dedicated to universal access, even though non-profit grassroots outlets require sustainable revenue.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The production operates cleanly across all planes with minimal friction. The minor tension exists on the Physical Plane between non-commercial open media and the financial necessity of ticketed platform distribution.

Social Physics Analysis:
Democracy Now! models a Smart Altruistic Maneuver. By prioritizing empowerment over institutional power and radical transparency over sanitized access, Goodman uses investigative journalism to resolve systemic silences rather than hoard influence.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Good. Independent adversarial reporting anchors public discourse in institutional accountability.

The Unavoidable Truth: Amy Goodman has built three decades of unmatched independent adversarial reporting.
The Unavoidable Lie: Corporate broadcast networks provide the same democratic scrutiny as non-profit journalism.

Alethekanon:
Independent media succeeds when it operates as a public trust rather than an access merchant. Documenting state overreach requires structural immunity from corporate advertising and political patronage.

Awwthekanon:
Amy Goodman has spent thirty years giving a microphone to people fighting for their lives, from East Timor to Standing Rock. Seeing her work honored reminds us how much courage it takes to speak truth with endless empathy.

Brothekanon:
Charging twenty bucks to stream a doc called 'Steal This Story' is hilarious irony, but let's be real: Amy Goodman has been putting corporate media talking heads to shame since the nineties. Total respect for keeping it independent.

Spirithekanon:
"Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute." Proverbs 31:8 PASS
By dedicating thirty years to giving voice to the silenced, independent journalism fulfills the timeless moral obligation to defend the vulnerable.

Amy Goodman is the host and executive producer of Democracy Now!, a national, daily, independent, award-winning news program airing on over 1,400 public television and radio stations worldwide.

The Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard honored Goodman with the 2014 I.F. Stone Medal for Journalistic Independence Lifetime Achievement Award. She is also the first journalist to receive the Right Livelihood Award, widely known as the 'Alternative Nobel Prize' for “developing an innovative model of truly independent grassroots political journalism that brings to millions of people the alternative voices that are often excluded by the mainstream media.” She is the first co-recipient of the Park Center for Independent Media’s Izzy Award, named for the great muckraking journalist I.F. Stone, and was later selected for induction into the Park Center’s I.F. Stone Hall of Fame. The Independent of London called Amy Goodman and Democracy Now! “an inspiration.”

Goodman has co-authored six New York Times bestsellers. Her latest, Democracy Now!: Twenty Years Covering the Movements Changing America, looks back over the past two decades of Democracy Now! and the powerful movements and charismatic leaders who are re-shaping our world. Before than, The Silenced Majority: Stories of Uprisings, Occupations, Resistance, and Hope, and Breaking the Sound Barrier, both written with Denis Moynihan, give voice to the many ordinary people standing up to corporate and government power. She co-authored her first three bestsellers with her brother, journalist David Goodman: Standing Up to the Madness: Ordinary Heroes in Extraordinary Times (2008), Static: Government Liars, Media Cheerleaders, and the People Who Fight Back (2006) and The Exception to the Rulers: Exposing Oily Politicians, War Profiteers, and the Media That Love Them (2004). She co-writes a weekly column with Denis Moynihan (also produced as an audio podcast) syndicated by King Features, for which she was recognized in 2007 with the James Aronson Award for Social Justice Reporting.

Goodman has received the Society for Professional Journalists Sigma Delta Chi Award for Excellence; American Women in Radio and Television Gracie Award; the Paley Center for Media’s She’s Made It Award; and the Puffin/Nation Prize for Creative Citizenship. Her reporting on East Timor and Nigeria has won numerous awards, including the George Polk Award, Robert F. Kennedy Prize for International Reporting, and the Alfred I. duPont-Columbia Award. Time Magazine named Democracy Now! its “Pick of the Podcasts,” along with NBC’s Meet the Press. PULSE named Goodman one of the 20 Top Global Media Figures of 2009.

She has also received awards from the Associated Press, United Press International, the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, and Project Censored. Goodman received the first ever Communication for Peace Award from the World Association for Christian Communication. She was also honored by the National Council of Teachers of English with the George Orwell Award for Distinguished Contribution to Honesty and Clarity in Public Language.
